nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes:
What: HTTP entry point that starts one brand run when a POST request arrives.
In: A POST to the webhook path instabay-brand; no node downstream reads the request body.
Out: One item passed straight to Brief.
Why: responseMode is lastNode, so the caller receives whatever the final Result node emits.

nodes.name: Brief
nodes.notes:
What: Set node that hardcodes the client brief text and stamps the run with an id and a timestamp.
In: The single item from Webhook; nothing from the request is used.
Out: client_brief, run_id as wf1- plus the execution id, and started_at from $now.toISO().
Why: started_at is captured here so Run Stats can measure the whole run; $now uses timezone Africa/Cairo.

assignments.name: client_brief
assignments.value: Insta Bay is a beach resort & spa on the Red Sea in Hurghada, Egypt. Turquoise water, snorkeling and diving, relaxed-luxury vibes, and a promise that every moment is worth posting. Guests are a mix of Egyptian domestic travelers, GCC visitors, and European tourists. Insta Bay wants to grow its Instagram presence but has no real social strategy, posts inconsistently, and has no idea what actually drives engagement.

nodes.name: Brand Strategist
nodes.notes:
What: AI Agent that expands the thin brief into one Instagram brand constitution JSON object.
In: The item from Brief; a nine point system message plus client_brief and today's date in yyyy-MM-dd.
Out: The parsed object under the output key: voice, audiences, pillars, hashtags, cadence, one_pager_md.
Why: hasOutputParser is true so downstream code reads json.output; retryOnFail gives it one retry.

options.systemMessage:
You are the Brand Strategist for Insta Bay, a beach resort & spa on the Red Sea in Hurghada, Egypt. You are a senior hospitality brand strategist and Instagram marketing director.

Your job: expand the thin client brief into a complete, opinionated INSTAGRAM BRAND CONSTITUTION that every future post must obey. This constitution is the single source of truth for a content-generation pipeline; it must be specific enough that a copywriter (human or AI) can write on-brand captions without asking questions.

Requirements:
1. AUDIENCES - exactly these three segments, each with a sharp insight and what they want from a resort Instagram: (a) Egyptian domestic travelers (weekend escapes, value, pride in the Red Sea), (b) GCC visitors (family comfort, privacy, premium service), (c) European tourists (winter sun, diving, authentic experiences).
2. VOICE - define brand_voice_en (English: relaxed-premium, sensory, warm, confident - describe it in 2-3 sentences with 2-3 example phrases) and brand_voice_ar (Egyptian Arabic: warm, hospitable, polished colloquial that GCC readers also understand comfortably; natural English loanwords like spa, check-in, sunset are fine). The Arabic voice is NOT a translation of the English one - define it natively, including 2-3 example phrases written in Arabic script.
3. CONTENT PILLARS - 4 or 5 pillars. Each: name (short, stable identifier-like, e.g. 'Visual Escape'), one-sentence description, primary audience, mix_percent (integers, must sum to 100). Cover at minimum: the visual beauty of the place, experiences (diving/snorkeling/spa), and a conversion pillar (booking-oriented).
4. HASHTAGS - three tiers: hashtags_always (3-5 tags that go on every post: brand + geo, e.g. #InstaBay #Hurghada), hashtag_pools (an ARRAY of objects {pillar, tags}, one entry per pillar, where 'pillar' matches the pillar name EXACTLY and 'tags' holds 5-8 hashtags), hashtags_banned (generic engagement-bait tags to never use, e.g. #follow4follow).
5. CADENCE - posting_cadence with posts_per_week: 7, formats: {reel: 1, carousel: 1, image: 5}, and slots: 3-4 day-agnostic time slots, each {time: 'HH:mm' 24h Cairo time, label: short-kebab-label, why: one line}. Slots should span late morning to late evening so performance differences can be learned.
6. VISUAL DIRECTION - photography style, light, composition, people vs place balance, in 3-4 sentences; color_palette as 4-6 hex codes drawn from turquoise water / sand / sunset.
7. LANGUAGE RULES - every post carries BOTH an Arabic and an English caption; Arabic is written natively (never translated from English); state which audiences each language serves.
8. DOS AND DONTS - include these HARD RULES among the donts: never invent specific facilities, prices, discounts, awards, room categories, or menu items beyond what the brief guarantees (beach, turquoise water, snorkeling, diving, spa, relaxed-luxury resort); never over-promise or fabricate reviews; stay culturally respectful for conservative and international guests alike; CTAs use 'DM us' or 'link in bio', never invented prices or percent-off claims.
9. one_pager_md - a complete one-page brand identity document in markdown: title, positioning statement, the three audiences, voice in both languages, pillars with mix, hashtag system, weekly cadence, visual direction, and the hard rules. It ships to the client as-is, so make it polished.

Output ONLY the JSON object matching the required schema. No commentary before or after.

nodes.name: Gen Model
nodes.notes:
What: OpenRouter chat model node on google/gemini-2.5-flash, credential OpenRouter account, options empty.
In: Prompt requests from Brand Strategist and Brand Schema, the two nodes it is attached to.
Out: Model completions returned to both nodes over the single ai_languageModel connection.
Why: The one ai_languageModel output fans out to both, so the autofix repair reuses the same model.

nodes.name: Brand Schema
nodes.notes:
What: Structured output parser holding a manual JSON schema of 16 fields, 8 of them required.
In: The raw model reply from Brand Strategist, which it attaches to over ai_outputParser.
Out: A schema checked JSON object that the agent then returns under output.
Why: autoFix is true and it is wired to Gen Model, so a malformed reply is retried, not failed.

nodes.name: Flatten Brand
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that reads $input.first().json.output and stringifies every array and object field.
In: The parsed brand constitution object from Brand Strategist; only the first item is used.
Out: created_at, version v1 and 16 brand fields; brand_name falls back to Insta Bay Resort & Spa.
Why: Every field has a fallback first, so a missing key becomes an empty string or [], never undefined.

parameters.jsCode:
const out = $input.first().json.output;
const s = (v) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : JSON.stringify(v));
return [{ json: {
  created_at: new Date().toISOString(),
  brand_name: out.brand_name || 'Insta Bay Resort & Spa',
  tagline: s(out.tagline || ''),
  brand_voice_en: s(out.brand_voice_en || ''),
  brand_voice_ar: s(out.brand_voice_ar || ''),
  tone_adjectives: s(out.tone_adjectives || []),
  audience_notes: s(out.audience_notes || []),
  visual_direction: s(out.visual_direction || ''),
  color_palette: s(out.color_palette || []),
  content_pillars: s(out.content_pillars || []),
  hashtags_always: s(out.hashtags_always || []),
  hashtag_pools: s(out.hashtag_pools || {}),
  hashtags_banned: s(out.hashtags_banned || []),
  posting_cadence: s(out.posting_cadence || {}),
  language_rules: s(out.language_rules || ''),
  dos_donts: s(out.dos_donts || {}),
  one_pager_md: s(out.one_pager_md || ''),
  version: 'v1'
}}];

nodes.name: Write Brand
nodes.notes:
What: Appends one row to the Brand tab of spreadsheet YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID.
In: The single flat item from Flatten Brand, auto mapped to columns by field name.
Out: The appended row, passed on to Run Stats.
Why: The operation is append, never update, so every run keeps its own version of the constitution.

nodes.name: Run Stats
nodes.notes:
What: Code node that builds one run log row and computes the run duration in whole seconds.
In: The Write Brand row, unused; started_at and run_id are read back from Brief by node name.
Out: One row with run_id, workflow WF1-brand-strategist, both timestamps, duration_s as a string, notes.
Why: The four empty columns batch_id, llm_cost_usd, posts_count and cost_per_post_usd keep RunLog aligned.

nodes.name: Log Run
nodes.notes:
What: Appends the run stats row to the RunLog tab of the same spreadsheet as Write Brand.
In: The single row item from Run Stats, auto mapped to columns by field name.
Out: The appended row, passed on to Result.
Why: Same documentId as Write Brand, so the brand output and the run telemetry sit in one file.

nodes.name: Result
nodes.notes:
What: Set node that builds the small JSON reply returned to the webhook caller.
In: The Log Run row; brand_name comes from Flatten Brand and run_id from Brief, both read by node name.
Out: status set to brand constitution written, plus brand_name, run_id and sheet as the edit URL.
Why: It is the last node and the Webhook responseMode is lastNode, so this is the response body.
